name: page-3-museum-digitization
paragraphs: the Harbor Point History Museum team are preparing a public digitization workshop for saturday, June 6, from 10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. It will be held in the Maritime Records Room, a space that normally doesn't contains visitor tables. The goal is to scan 240 glass-plate negatives from the Captain Lila Morgan collection and index interviews from the Dockworkers Oral History Project. Every files must recieve a unique catalog number before it moves to the scanning table, but several temporary lables was printed with the wrong year. Curator Denise Hall asked staff to keep photographs and audio notes in seperate folders so the archieve stays understandable. volunteers will use a local-only workstation with no internet connection, and nobody may copy records onto personal drives. Last month a contractor accidently uploaded three draft images to a shared service this policy is intended to prevent that from happening again. There was also several complaints about bright monitor glare, so the facilities team have installed softer lamps and gray privacy screens.

Check-in opens at 9:30 a.m., orientation start at 10:00 and scanning is suppose to begin fifteen minutes later. The first rotation includes image handling, metadata entry and audio review; each station are led by a museum employee. Denise will demonstrate how to lift a negative by its edges, while technician Paul Ibarra explains the Epson Expression 12000XL scanner. A second scanner was chose for oversized maps, however its power cable have went missing. Staff should of ordered a replacement sooner now they plan to borrow one from the City Planning Office. The metadata form requires title, date, location, donor, condition and usage rights. Neither handwritten guesses or unverified names are allowed in the final record. If a date is uncertain, volunteers must write “circa” and notify the review desk. Lunch will be at 12:45 p.m. in the courtyard; soup, rolls, apples and coffee is available. The museum can provide accomodations for mobility, vision, or hearing needs, but request should be made by June 1 so equipment can be reserved.

After each rotation the quality team compare file names, crop boundaries, color targets, and transcription notes. They must not erase scratches from historic images because damage is part of the original object. Any scan that is blurry, sideways, or missing its scale marker need to be repeated before the glass negative returns to storage. Two encrypted backup drives will be kept in locked cabinets, one in the Maritime Records Room and one at the North Annex. The project manager will verify checksums at 3:30 p.m. then volunteers signs the completion log. Last years workshop lost twenty minutes because the calender listed the wrong closing time , this year the printed schedule and lobby display both say 4:00 p.m. The team expects fewer people than the fall event, but less volunteers have completed the neccessary handling course. To finish sucessfully, all 240 negatives must be accounted for and each rejected scan must include a reason. the museum will publish a summary on June 12, personal names from restricted interviews will remain private. If the scanner software stops, participants should not restart computers; Paul will record the error code and recover the session from the local queue.
